## Verdict

wrong

## Bearer

None single — the fix changes twenty-one independent await/suspend call
sites across four modules, none of them called by another. Grouped by
file:

Play Services Wearable (`core-sync`):
- `link/WearableLinkStateSource.kt:67` — `addLocalCapability(CAPABILITY_NAME).await()`
- `link/WearableLinkStateSource.kt:68` — `nodeClient.localNode.await()`
- `link/WearableLinkStateSource.kt:72` — `getCapability(CAPABILITY_NAME, FILTER_REACHABLE).await()`
- `transport/MessageChannel.kt:37` — `connectedNodes.await()`
- `transport/MessageChannel.kt:39` — `sendMessage(nodeId, path, data).await()`

Health Services (`app-wear`, `sensor/session/ExerciseSessionSystemImpl.kt`
unless noted):
- `:45` — `getCurrentExerciseInfoAsync().await()`
- `:87` — `getCapabilitiesAsync().await()`, called both from `availableDataTypes()` (`:30`) and from `startExerciseSession()` (`:55`)
- `:59` — `startExerciseAsync(config).await()`
- `:67` — `endExerciseAsync().await()`
- `:79` — `overrideBatchingModesForActiveExerciseAsync(overrides).await()`
- `sensor/reading/SensorReadingsSource.kt:75` — `unregisterMeasureCallbackAsync(...).await()`

Health Connect (`app-phone`):
- `health/HrHistoryReaderImpl.kt:37` — `client.readRecords(...)`
- `health/permission/HrPermissionSystemImpl.kt:32` — `permissionController.getGrantedPermissions()`
- `health/permission/HrPermissionSystemImpl.kt:38` — `deferred.await()`

Room (`core-data` and `app-wear`):
- `profile/ProfileRepositoryImpl.kt:108-114` — `observe()`'s `.catch`
- `race/RaceRepositoryImpl.kt:143` — `observeAll()`
- `race/RaceRepositoryImpl.kt:152` — `observeReference()`
- `sync/WatchHistoryStoreImpl.kt:25` — `observe()`
- `app-wear/.../race/RaceRecordingRepositoryImpl.kt:218` — `observeRecorded()`
- Every `withContext(Dispatchers.IO) { runCatching { ... } }` suspend surface of `RaceRepositoryImpl`, `ProfileRepositoryImpl` and `RaceRecordingRepositoryImpl` — `markSegment`, `undoLastMark`, `stopRace`, `markSent`, `findInProgress`, `eraseRecorded` and their siblings, all sharing the same shape
- `sync/WatchHistoryStoreImpl.kt:21` — `replaceAll()`

`SensorReadingsSource.registerOne()` (`:109`),
`SensorPermissionSystemImpl.requestPermission()`'s
`deferred.await()` (`:87-90`) and
`ConnectivityPermissionSystemImpl.requestPermission()`'s
`deferred.await()` (`:57-58`) are excluded from this list: they carry the
same missing-timeout defect but are reported and fixed as their own gap.

## Trigger

Each site fires on its own existing caller, already observed today: the
device-link check on app start (`WearableLinkStateSource`), a race
push/pull (`MessageChannel`), opening or closing an exercise session and
reading its capabilities (`ExerciseSessionSystemImpl`), unregistering a
sensor callback (`SensorReadingsSource`), reading heart-rate history and
requesting the heart-rate permission on the Profile screen
(`HrHistoryReaderImpl`, `HrPermissionSystemImpl`), and every read or write
the repositories perform on the Room database. None of these triggers is
new; only the absence of a bound on the wait is common to all of them.

## Today

None of the twenty-one calls listed under `## Bearer` is wrapped in
`withTimeoutOrNull` or `withTimeout`. Each either suspends on a
`Task`/`ListenableFuture` bridged through `suspendCancellableCoroutine`
(the Play Services and Health Services calls), on a Health Connect
client call, or on a Room DAO call inside `runCatching`/`.catch` — and in
every one of them the wait resolves only when the underlying platform,
store or dependency responds, however long that takes. The only two
`withTimeoutOrNull` calls in the project, `NavigationModule.kt:44` and
`:49`, bound a `Flow.first()` read of state already held in the process;
they do not bound any of the calls above.

Three of the twenty-one, in `HrPermissionSystemImpl.kt:37-38`
(`launcher.launch(...)` then `deferred.await()`), share the shape of the
two permission-system waits fixed as their own gap: the `deferred` is
completed only by `onPermissionResult()`, called from the system
dialog's callback. If the hosting activity is destroyed before that
callback fires, the `deferred` is never completed and the coroutine
awaiting it suspends for the remainder of the process's life — the same
defect, on a third file the other gap's report does not name.

## Expected

Each of the twenty-one calls is wrapped in a timeout sized to what it
does — a device-link or capability read, a Health Services call, a
Health Connect call, a Room read or write — and a timeout is treated as
an ordinary failure of that call, not a crash: logged, and turned into
the same declared failure value or state the call already returns or
would return on any other failure, exactly as `MessageChannel.kt:37-39`
already does for every other failure and only lacks for the timeout
itself.

`HrPermissionSystemImpl.requestPermission()`'s `deferred.await()`
additionally needs the same treatment already required for the other two
infinite permission waits: on timeout, `requestPermission()` returns a
declined permission instead of leaving the coroutine suspended, and the
pending callback registration is cleared so a dialog response arriving
after the timeout does not resolve a `deferred` nobody still awaits.
